question: A GraphQL query for 50 posts, each with its author, takes two seconds. The database log shows 51 queries for one request. What is the usual fix?
context: Each field has its own resolver. The author resolver runs SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? for the post it is given.

options.label: Batch the author lookups per request, loading all 50 in one query
options.why: The resolvers are fine individually; they are simply called once per post. A per-request loader collects the ids asked for in one tick and issues one WHERE id IN (…) query, then hands each resolver its row. Fifty-one queries become two, and resolvers stay simple.

options.label: Put a Redis cache in front of the users table for the author lookups
options.why: Fifty-one round trips become fifty-one cache round trips, which is faster but still fifty-one. The shape of the problem — one call per item — is unchanged, and a cache brings invalidation with it.

options.label: Replace the GraphQL endpoint with REST routes built for each screen
options.why: A hand-written endpoint can join posts and authors in one query, but so can a batched resolver without giving up the API. Changing the protocol is a large fix for a data-loading pattern.

options.label: Add an index on users.id so each of the fifty lookups runs faster
options.why: users.id is the primary key and already indexed. Each query is fast; there are simply fifty of them, each paying a network round trip and a planning step.
